correctness.rationale: The exact primal volume follows from sign-orthant decomposition of a reflected simplex and beta integration. The polar formula uses the full 2(n+1) support inequalities, vertical fibers, exact sum-zero gap Jacobian and a disjoint chamber partition. Strict positivity of the second derivative of log-polar-volume and vertex-permutation symmetry prove the unique global Santaló minimizer. The n(1-z_n)→2 and e limit follow by a uniform compact-s expansion and derivative sign trapping. The included standalone program independently reconstructs primal hulls and polar halfspace intersections for n=2..6, with 35 successful numerical volume comparisons, and checks n=2 radicals. Finite checks are corroboration, not the universal proof. Primary assumptions are regularity, normalization, n≥2 and |z|<1.

The reflected-simplex formula does yield the horizontal section volumes used as an input to the primal-volume proof, but leaves the new axial polar fiber integral, its strictly convex logarithmic profile, and the limiting factor e unproved. The central-polytope volume formula and standard Santaló existence cannot imply the exact Cayley-body result by specialization or affine equivalence as the studied vertex configurations and dimensions differ. In particular the new polar profile requires all n+1 ordered gaps and the height fiber simultaneously.

originality.rationale: The claim completes a natural quantitative problem for the 2026 canonical regular-simplex Cayley construction: exact off-center polar-volume profile, unique noncentral Santaló point, and sharp asymptotic factor e against the simplex reference product. The inspected motivating face-lattice theorems do not calculate volume; the closest relevant published exact Santaló formula is for a horizontal reflected-simplex Minkowski sum, not the two-level Cayley hull. Actual targeted similarity searches and primary-literature comparisons found no dominating statement. Historical priority remains independently unverified; absence of a search hit is not used as a proof.

value.rationale: The exact best volume product is a natural sharp invariant of the explicit bipolar-cube realization newly identified in a 2026 geometric construction. The optimizer is unexpectedly off the axial midpoint at every n≥2 and approaches the polar-simplex end with n(1-z_n)→2, despite constant cubical combinatorics. The full profile and nontrivial asymptotic ratio e to the simplex benchmark give an interpretable high-dimensional geometric comparison, without asserting arbitrary-cube optimality.
